claims.text: Peer-reviewed work attributed to this researcher evaluated MAP of Serbian-grown raspberries at 2 °C over 14 days across three gas compositions, monitoring firmness, colour, soluble solids, titratable acidity and visual mould incidence plus Botrytis cinerea counts.
limitations: Results are at lab/experimental scale under controlled 2 °C storage, not on commercial export consignments.
Abstract-level report only; film OTR/CO₂TR of the tested films is not stated in the retrieved excerpt.

claims.text: The reported raspberry MAP study found that a 5% O₂/15% CO₂ atmosphere reduced Botrytis incidence by 63% relative to an ambient-air control and maintained firmness above commercial thresholds for 12 days versus 6 days in air, with sensory marketability at day 10 under optimal MAP.
limitations: 63% reduction is relative to control, so it does not imply sub-1% absolute mould incidence by day 14.
Sensor panel marketability at day 10 falls short of the company's 14-day target.

claims.text: Related work attributed to this researcher screened 12 commercial films differing in OTR and CO₂TR for mixed-berry trays at 2 °C and used finite-element gas-permeation modelling to confirm headspace trends and predict equilibrium under alternative fill weights; one film (OTR 3,800, CO₂TR 18,000 cm³/m²/day) kept headspace within acceptable ranges for three species and cut mould incidence 55% versus a polyethylene control.
limitations: The tray was mixed-berry, not raspberry-only 125 g rPET punnet geometry.
Film specification values are reported as study findings and cannot be transferred to the company's punnet without local verification.

claims.text: The researcher's raspberry MAP study also examined pre-cooling before sealing: forced-air cooling reached target core temperature in 38 minutes versus 210 minutes for room cooling, gave 14 hours earlier headspace O₂ equilibration, and was linked to significantly lower Botrytis incidence and better firmness at day 8; hydrocooling produced excess free moisture and calyx decay.
limitations: Findings concern pre-cooling protocols at 2 °C experimental scale; applicability to the company's packing-house line is unverified.
Day-8 outcomes do not demonstrate day-14 performance.

claims.text: Attributed work translates cold-chain data into shelf-life prediction: a 12-month digital-twin pilot on Serbian berry consignments flagged 88% of consignments later showing elevated spoilage with 9% false positives, and a Monte Carlo stochastic model propagating temperature variability from 180 monitored consignments covered 91% of observed outcomes, identifying mean transport temperature and door-opening frequency as the dominant variance drivers.
limitations: The stochastic framework is demonstrated on strawberries and total aerobic count; Botrytis-specific calibration on raspberries is separate.
Modelling addresses prediction and prioritisation, not film selection by itself.

claims.text: A book chapter attributed to this researcher covers gas mass-balance modelling, film permeability selection, tray-geometry effects on headspace equilibration, and linkage of predictive microbiology to temperature-monitoring data, with a worked example of a forced-air pre-cooling and MAP line for a mid-sized raspberry exporter.
limitations: A textbook chapter is a methodological reference, not validation for FreshPak's specific punnet.

claims.text: The combination of raspberry-specific MAP gas-mix results, film OTR/CO₂TR screening with permeation modelling, and temperature-driven Botrytis prediction plausibly covers the modelling gap FreshPak describes: converting measured OTR/CO₂TR and headspace data into a film specification for its 125 g rPET punnet at 2–4 °C.
limitations: No retrieved evidence shows work on heat-sealed anti-fog lidding film on 125 g rPET shells or on micro-condensation control specifically.
Semantic support of evidence for this challenge is unassessed; fit is inferred from abstract-level content.

claims.text: Because the identified evidence is experimental and modelling-based rather than a validated commercial 14-day packing-house protocol, the realistic contribution is a bounded film-specification and trial-design study, not a guaranteed one-percent mould outcome.
limitations: The company's own two-season logs and two failed film grades are unexamined here; data quality is unknown.

claims.text: Proposed pilot contribution: use FreshPak's OTR/CO₂TR and headspace measurements plus its two seasons of temperature, humidity and inspection data to (1) estimate raspberry respiration-driven target atmosphere at 2–4 °C, (2) rank a small set of candidate lidding films by modelled steady-state headspace and Botrytis risk, and (3) co-design a compact simulated-transit trial matrix.
limitations: Film candidates, data formats and lab-turnaround capacity must be confirmed with FreshPak.
Any timeline or number of candidate films is an assumption to agree, not a source fact.

claims.text: Suggested milestones and go/no-go logic: baseline the current film and seal setting in simulated transit (mould incidence at day 9 and 14); measure headspace O₂/CO₂ and respiration for 1–3 proposed films; compare observed headspace against model predictions; proceed to a pre-season consignment check only if the best candidate meets an agreed mould-incidence and headspace-target threshold; otherwise revise the film or add pre-cooling/condensation measures.
limitations: Thresholds, replicates and consignment counts are proposals requiring agreement; the <1% day-14 target is the company's stated goal, not a demonstrated result.
Budget limits preclude a large external programme, so replicate counts may be constrained.

limitations: No restriction blocks this topic, but the exact form of engagement (sponsored project, PhD co-supervision, consultancy terms) is not specified.
Profile-level industry experience is self-described and not independently detailed in evidence.

claims.text: Unresolved questions include whether the visible mould arises from field inoculum, pre-cooling delay, condensation, or atmosphere imbalance; how seal integrity and anti-fog film behaviour interact with micro-condensation on this rPET shell; and whether simulated transit will reproduce the real German/Netherlands destination outcomes.
limitations: These questions follow from source content as gaps, not from experimental data on FreshPak's product.

summary.text: Dr. Jelena Marković (R0976) is a strong partial match for C036-CH1: her attributed work covers raspberry MAP gas composition for Serbian export, film OTR/CO₂TR screening with permeation modelling, pre-cooling effects on Botrytis, and temperature-driven shelf-life prediction on real Serbian consignments. This addresses the modelling gap and the film-specification translation the company lacks, but it does not by itself guarantee <1% mould at day 14; a bounded trial is the appropriate next step.

technicalRationale.text: Raspberry-specific evidence: a 5% O₂/15% CO₂ atmosphere cut Botrytis incidence 63% versus air and held firmness for 12 days at 2 °C, giving a defensible starting point for atmosphere targets.

Film specification capability: 12-film OTR/CO₂TR screening with finite-element gas-permeation modelling shows a method to convert measured permeability and headspace data into a candidate specification, matching the company's stated need to translate OTR/CO₂TR numbers into a film grade.

Condensation and pre-cooling: evidence on forced-air versus room cooling and hydrocooling links equilibration speed and free moisture to Botrytis incidence, relevant to the company's micro-condensation hypothesis.

Cold-chain data use: existing work ingesting temperature/humidity streams into Botrytis-relevant prediction models indicates usable methodology for FreshPak's two seasons of logs and destination inspection reports.

cooperationScope.text: Scope: a film-specification and trial-design project using FreshPak's lab (OTR/CO₂TR, headspace gas, seal strength) and historic shipment data, with milestones (a) translation of logs into a temperature/humidity profile, (b) modelled headspace and Botrytis risk ranking for a short candidate film list, (c) simulated-transit trial protocol and its execution, (d) pre-season consignment check.
Engagement form to agree: joint project and/or industrial PhD co-supervision, consistent with the researcher's stated openness.

validation.text: Baseline: current lidding film and seal pressure run in the simulated-transit protocol, recording visible Botrytis incidence at days 9 and 14 and headspace O₂/CO₂. Candidate films are measured the same way, with model-predicted versus observed equilibrium gas composition compared per film and fill weight. Go/no-go: advance to the pre-season consignment check only if the best candidate reaches the agreed mould-incidence threshold and its observed headspace trend is consistent with the model; otherwise revise film, seal setting or pre-cooling before the season deadline.

constraints.text: Required inputs from FreshPak: the two current film grades and their measured OTR/CO₂TR, standard punnet geometry and fill weight, seal pressure range, two seasons of temperature/humidity logs and destination inspection reports, and lab time for headspace and seal testing. Engagement is limited to the researcher's lab and part-time involvement; no large external testing programme can be assumed given the stated budget.

What remains outside the supported scope: heat-seal and anti-fog film behaviour, micro-condensation control in the 125 g rPET shell, compostable-material migration, and full commercial deployment or a contractual one-percent mould guarantee.

unknowns.text: Open questions: which factor dominates visible mould (field inoculum, pre-cooling delay, condensation, atmosphere imbalance); how anti-fog chemistry and seal integrity interact with condensation; whether simulated transit reproduces German/Netherlands destination outcomes; and whether any candidate film can reach <1% at day 14 within budget.

findings.explanation: R0926 (Sofija Ristić, ranked 3) is a mechanical-engineering sealing-systems researcher whose registered corpus concerns elastomeric gaskets, O-rings and IP-rated electromechanical/enclosure housings: condensation inside sealed electrical enclosures (E014, E072), moisture ingress through compressed gaskets in IP54 steel cabinets (E012), FIP vs EPDM gaskets on electrical cabinets (E094). Her project MOISTMOD targets low-voltage electrical enclosure condensation modelling with a Python prediction tool (E007, E142). There is no registered Evidence of perishable-food, berry, MAP or food-packaging work, and her industry experience is enclosure/cabinet manufacturers (E127). Keyword overlap ('condensation', 'sealed', 'modelling') therefore does not establish technical suitability for Botrytis control in raspberry punnets; her 'modelling' expertise is heat-moisture transfer in non-food cavities, not respiration/permeability-based MAP design.
findings.recheckQuestion: Does R0926 have any registered Evidence of fresh-produce or food-packaging MAP work, as opposed to electromechanical enclosure condensation?

findings.explanation: R0426 (Aleksandar Bošković, ranked 4) contributes injection-moulding thermomechanical simulation: warpage/residual stress in PA6 and PP parts, mould heat-transfer-coefficient calibration and cooling-circuit CFD (E100, E172, E002, E108, E016, E111). His sole condensation-related item is a co-authored enclosure simulation (E014), not food packaging. The only keyword link to the challenge is the word 'mould' (mould tooling, not Botrytis mould). His project is semi-crystalline injection-moulding warpage (E177, E148) and his industry work is automotive plastics (E163); restrictions require partners to supply moulded parts and licences for proprietary simulation software (E176, E148). Nothing registered supports thermoformed rPET punnet/lidding-film or fruit-spoilage work, so lexical agreement on 'mould' is a false lead.
findings.recheckQuestion: Is there any registered Evidence that R0426 has worked on food packaging, thermoformed trays or microbial spoilage rather than injection-moulding warpage?

findings.explanation: R0715 (Bojan Grbić, ranked 2) is strong on heat-seal science — mLLDPE seal-initiation temperature, seal-layer formulation, peel vs burst acceptance, film ageing (E131/E102, E146, E047, E039, E027, E134, patent E045/E145) — but no registered Evidence addresses fruit, respiration-matched OTR, headspace gas composition or Botrytis. The evidence explicitly frames his work as VFFS film sealability (E150, E122) and the patent example is cited in the pool's own field pointers only via shared generic terms ('heat','seal','film','temperature'); the actual documents are about thermal sealing windows, not mould control. Additionally his notes state a preference for collaborations with access to production-scale extrusion equipment because his cast-film line cannot replicate industrial conditions (E110), and his open_to items are framed around seal-layer formulation with converters/resin suppliers (E008) — a partial mismatch with a converter that only needs film specification and punnets, not seal-layer R&D. His sealing contribution would be secondary at best and ranking him second overstates fit.
findings.recheckQuestion: Does any registered Evidence show R0715 applying seal or permeability expertise to fresh-produce spoilage outcomes?

findings.explanation: R0172 (Snežana Puzović, ranked 5) is the best-substantiated permeability/film-transport expert (OTR/WVTR vs temperature, E086, E168, E070, E135, E126, patent E024/E076). However her registered notes state she is available for new collaborations only from autumn 2026 onwards while finishing MONOBAR supervision commitments (E173), which conflicts with the challenge's roughly eight-month pre-next-season deadline and its need for trial work now. She also prefers that experimental work be conducted in her own laboratory (E173), while her open_to centres on barrier characterisation and measurement services rather than MAP specification for a berry exporter (E179, E128). Any plan relying on her for near-term simulated-transit trials must be checked against this start date.
findings.recheckQuestion: Can R0172 start before autumn 2026, and would she accept a scope centred on film-specification modelling rather than pure barrier characterisation?

findings.explanation: R0786 (Svetlana Sabo, ranked 6) is a hygrothermal-modelling and enclosure-physics specialist: condensation onset in polycarbonate/ABS housings, dew-point margins, cable-gland vapour ingress in electrical substation cabinets and thermostat/housing seal physics (E035, E118, E034, E049, E003, E083, E106). Her industry experience is outdoor metering cabinets and product certification disputes (E160), and her open_to is enclosure design for moisture control (E038). No registered Evidence involves packaged food, MAP, respiration-driven gas exchange or Botrytis. The shared terms 'sealed', 'condensation' and 'humidity' describe water-vapour behaviour in electronic housings with heat sources — a fundamentally different transport regime from micro-condensation inside a small sealed punnet driven by berry respiration. Treating her as a condensation expert for raspberry punnets would extrapolate beyond her evidence.
findings.recheckQuestion: Has R0786 ever worked on condensation inside food or produce packaging rather than electrical enclosures?

findings.explanation: R1044 (Branka Lalić, ranked 7) is scheduled for parental leave from October 2026 to approximately April 2027 (E004), which overlaps the deadline-critical window the challenge describes; only commitments starting before October 2026 can be accommodated. Her registered output is biopolymer/starch–protein reactive extrusion with property mapping including OTR (E117, E182, patent E125) and some co-authorship on seal-test work (E039, E134 via shared documents), but no registered Evidence covers fruit, Botrytis or produce MAP. Her open_to is biopolymer formulation/testing (E165) and the twin-screw line is limited to ~5 kg/h, constraining any punnet-scale prototyping (E004). Relevance to the stated film-grade/OTR-matching problem is peripheral.
findings.recheckQuestion: Would R1044's group add anything to rPET lidding-film specification within the eight-month window, and can work start before her October 2026 leave?

findings.explanation: R0084 (Petar Dobanovački, ranked 8) is a mechanical-testing/accelerated-ageing specialist for engineering and biomedical polymers: hygroscopic swelling of PEI parts, PA12 fatigue after humidity cycling, TPU catheter ageing (E099, E068, E137, E120). His only film-related link is being participant index 1 on the PERMTEMP permeability project (E017, E115), whose subject is a permeability reference dataset for polyolefin films (an instrument calibration/reference dataset rather than MAP design). Profile bio is empty and his industry experience is medical-device and compounding companies (E044); open_to is fatigue/ageing testing, climate chamber, CMM and medical-device certification consulting (E042). No registered Evidence supports Berry/Botrytis or produce-packaging work, so his rank-8 inclusion rests on shared words in a shared project.
findings.recheckQuestion: Does R0084 have any registered Evidence of produce-packaging or spoilage work beyond the shared PERMTEMP project participation?

findings.explanation: Reviewing the whole pool, the substantive raspberry/Botrytis/MAP content is concentrated almost entirely in R0976 (Jelena Marković): Serbian raspberry MAP gas-mix specifications with 14-day storage and Botrytis incidence (E138), pre-cooling and headspace equilibration effects on Botrytis (E073), OTR/CO₂TR film selection for small-format berry trays with finite-element gas-permeation modelling (E087), Botrytis predictive-model/digital-twin work (E040, E064), and MAP engineering design (E055). The remaining seven candidates' registered Evidence contains no berry-Botrytis outcome data, so a portfolio that treats several of them as equivalent berry-spoilage experts would rest on keyword proximity only. Note also that the pool is truncated (40 merged, 8 selected) with SEMANTIC_SUPPORT_UNASSESSED and NARROW_CHANNEL_COVERAGE; absence of contrary evidence for unselected researchers cannot be assumed. This is advisory, not a verdict on any final team, and does not constitute approval.
findings.recheckQuestion: If any candidate other than R0976 is presented as bringing berry-Botrytis outcome evidence, which registered Evidence ID supplies it?

findings.explanation: Only the eight fixed-pool candidates and their registered Evidence were inspected. No claim could be cited for the Proposer's (unseen) claims, so claimIds are empty throughout. Checks of the remaining 32 merged candidates, of whether any candidate's Evidence contains conflicting results, and of whether the challenge's sub-1% mould target is achievable by any candidate were not performed; the challenge text itself notes that two prior film-grade/seal-pressure trials did not reduce mould rates enough, which is a customer-stated constraint on expected effect size rather than candidate counter-evidence.
findings.recheckQuestion: Should the remaining merged candidates be inspected before any portfolio finalisation?

noCounterEvidenceFound: No blocking incompatibility was found between R0976's registered Evidence and the challenge's raspberry/Botrytis/MAP needs; no absent-attribution issue was found for any of the eight candidates (unattributedEvidenceIds empty, all content links backed by identity Evidence).
No explicit identity conflict (duplicate or contradictory researcher identity bindings) was found for any of the eight inspected candidates.

No counter-evidence was found indicating that the challenge's stated OTR/CO₂TR and headspace-measurement capability is incompatible with the pool's registered permeability instrumentation descriptions; this was not a proof of suitability, only that no contradiction appeared in inspected records.

findings.explanation: The draft's quantitative summaries match the original abstracts: E138 states the 5% O₂/15% CO₂ atmosphere reduced Botrytis incidence by 63% vs control, firmness above threshold 12 days vs 6 days, and marketability at day 10; C2 reports these figures and explicitly limits them ('relative to control, does not imply sub-1% absolute', 'sensory panel day 10 falls short of 14-day target'). E073 reports 38 vs 210 min cooling, 14 h earlier O₂ equilibration, lower Botrytis at day 8; C4 carries the same numbers and notes day-8 outcomes do not demonstrate day-14 performance. No overstated universal or deployment claim is present.
findings.recheckQuestion: Do the quoted numerical results in C2 and C4 remain identical to the values in E138 and E073?

findings.explanation: C3 attributes the 12-film OTR/CO₂TR screening, finite-element permeation modelling and 55% mould reduction to E087, and E140 confirms R0976 is author 3 on that record. The draft's limitation notes that the tray was mixed-berry and that the film spec (OTR 3,800, CO₂TR 18,000) cannot be transferred to the company's 125 g rPET punnet without local verification. The inference is therefore properly bounded; it does not claim the company's punnet will achieve the same result.
findings.recheckQuestion: Does C3 avoid asserting transferability of the mixed-berry film specification to the 125 g rPET punnet beyond local verification?

findings.explanation: C5's digital-twin figures (88% flagged, 9% false positives, four exporters, 240 consignments) match E040, and the Monte Carlo 91% coverage and 180 consignments match E064. E064 is on strawberry total aerobic count, and the draft says so in its limitation and notes that Botrytis-specific raspberry calibration is separate. This is honestly labelled and does not overstate the evidence as validated raspberry Botrytis prediction.
findings.recheckQuestion: Is the strawberry/aerobic-count basis of the Monte Carlo model disclosed and kept separate from Botrytis-specific prediction in the draft?

findings.explanation: E055 is a book chapter covering gas mass balance, film permeability selection, tray geometry effects on headspace equilibration and a worked forced-air pre-cooling + MAP example for a mid-sized raspberry exporter; C6 reproduces this and correctly frames it as a methodological reference, not validation. The technicalRationale line linked to C4 ('links equilibration speed and free moisture to Botrytis incidence, relevant to the company's micro-condensation hypothesis') stays within what E073 supports (hydrocooling free moisture promoting calyx decay) without claiming micro-condensation control is proven.
findings.recheckQuestion: Does the technicalRationale for C4 avoid claiming demonstrated micro-condensation control in the 125 g rPET punnet?

findings.explanation: The proposal sections correctly refuse to guarantee the customer's <1% day-14 target (C8, constraints, unknowns), describe a bounded film-specification/trial-design contribution grounded in the candidate's registered MAP/film/cold-chain work (C9, C10), and state the participation form as joint project and/or industrial PhD supervision consistent with E101/E015. C11's claim of prior work with three fruit exporters matches E015 verbatim, and the section correctly notes the exact engagement form is not specified. This meets the cooperation-support requirement with registered evidence of a concrete contribution to the core modelling gap, without implying unlimited availability, guaranteed success or completed deployment.
findings.recheckQuestion: Does the proposal continue to state the <1% day-14 outcome as the company's goal rather than a demonstrated result, and to confine the contribution to registered MAP/film/cold-chain competence?

claims.text: Peer-reviewed work attributed to this researcher evaluated MAP of Serbian-grown raspberries at 2 °C over 14 days across three gas compositions, monitoring firmness, colour, soluble solids, titratable acidity and visual mould incidence plus Botrytis cinerea counts.
limitations: Results are at lab/experimental scale under controlled 2 °C storage, not on commercial export consignments.
Abstract-level report only; film OTR/CO₂TR of the tested films is not stated in the retrieved excerpt.

claims.text: The reported raspberry MAP study found that a 5% O₂/15% CO₂ atmosphere reduced Botrytis incidence by 63% relative to an ambient-air control and maintained firmness above commercial thresholds for 12 days versus 6 days in air, with sensory marketability at day 10 under optimal MAP.
limitations: 63% reduction is relative to control, so it does not imply sub-1% absolute mould incidence by day 14.
Sensor panel marketability at day 10 falls short of the company's 14-day target.

claims.text: Related work attributed to this researcher screened 12 commercial films differing in OTR and CO₂TR for mixed-berry trays at 2 °C and used finite-element gas-permeation modelling to confirm headspace trends and predict equilibrium under alternative fill weights; one film (OTR 3,800, CO₂TR 18,000 cm³/m²/day) kept headspace within acceptable ranges for three species and cut mould incidence 55% versus a polyethylene control.
limitations: The tray was mixed-berry, not raspberry-only 125 g rPET punnet geometry.
Film specification values are reported as study findings and cannot be transferred to the company's punnet without local verification.

claims.text: The researcher's raspberry MAP study also examined pre-cooling before sealing: forced-air cooling reached target core temperature in 38 minutes versus 210 minutes for room cooling, gave 14 hours earlier headspace O₂ equilibration, and was linked to significantly lower Botrytis incidence and better firmness at day 8; hydrocooling produced excess free moisture and calyx decay.
limitations: Findings concern pre-cooling protocols at 2 °C experimental scale; applicability to the company's packing-house line is unverified.
Day-8 outcomes do not demonstrate day-14 performance.

claims.text: Attributed work translates cold-chain data into shelf-life prediction: a 12-month digital-twin pilot on Serbian berry consignments flagged 88% of consignments later showing elevated spoilage with 9% false positives, and a Monte Carlo stochastic model propagating temperature variability from 180 monitored consignments covered 91% of observed outcomes, identifying mean transport temperature and door-opening frequency as the dominant variance drivers.
limitations: The stochastic framework is demonstrated on strawberries and total aerobic count; Botrytis-specific calibration on raspberries is separate.
Modelling addresses prediction and prioritisation, not film selection by itself.

claims.text: A book chapter attributed to this researcher covers gas mass-balance modelling, film permeability selection, tray-geometry effects on headspace equilibration, and linkage of predictive microbiology to temperature-monitoring data, with a worked example of a forced-air pre-cooling and MAP line for a mid-sized raspberry exporter.
limitations: A textbook chapter is a methodological reference, not validation for FreshPak's specific punnet.

limitations: No retrieved evidence shows work on heat-sealed anti-fog lidding film on 125 g rPET shells or on micro-condensation control specifically.
Semantic support of evidence for this challenge is unassessed; fit is inferred from abstract-level content.

limitations: The company's own two-season logs and two failed film grades are unexamined here; data quality is unknown.

claims.text: Proposed pilot contribution: use FreshPak's OTR/CO₂TR and headspace measurements plus its two seasons of temperature, humidity and inspection data to (1) estimate raspberry respiration-driven target atmosphere at 2–4 °C, (2) rank a small set of candidate lidding films by modelled steady-state headspace and Botrytis risk, and (3) co-design a compact simulated-transit trial matrix.
limitations: Film candidates, data formats and lab-turnaround capacity must be confirmed with FreshPak.
Any timeline or number of candidate films is an assumption to agree, not a source fact.

claims.text: Suggested milestones and go/no-go logic: baseline the current film and seal setting in simulated transit (mould incidence at day 9 and 14); measure headspace O₂/CO₂ and respiration for 1–3 proposed films; compare observed headspace against model predictions; proceed to a pre-season consignment check only if the best candidate meets an agreed mould-incidence and headspace-target threshold; otherwise revise the film or add pre-cooling/condensation measures.
limitations: Thresholds, replicates and consignment counts are proposals requiring agreement; the <1% day-14 target is the company's stated goal, not a demonstrated result.
Budget limits preclude a large external programme, so replicate counts may be constrained.

limitations: These questions follow from source content as gaps, not from experimental data on FreshPak's product.

summary.text: Dr. Jelena Marković (R0976) is a strong partial match for C036-CH1: her attributed work covers raspberry MAP gas composition for Serbian export, film OTR/CO₂TR screening with permeation modelling, pre-cooling effects on Botrytis, and temperature-driven shelf-life prediction on real Serbian consignments. This addresses the modelling gap and the film-specification translation the company lacks, but it does not by itself guarantee <1% mould at day 14; a bounded trial is the appropriate next step.

technicalRationale.text: Raspberry-specific evidence: a 5% O₂/15% CO₂ atmosphere cut Botrytis incidence 63% versus air and held firmness for 12 days at 2 °C, giving a defensible starting point for atmosphere targets.

Film specification capability: 12-film OTR/CO₂TR screening with finite-element gas-permeation modelling shows a method to convert measured permeability and headspace data into a candidate specification, matching the company's stated need to translate OTR/CO₂TR numbers into a film grade.

Condensation and pre-cooling: evidence on forced-air versus room cooling and hydrocooling links equilibration speed and free moisture to Botrytis incidence, relevant to the company's micro-condensation hypothesis.

Cold-chain data use: existing work ingesting temperature/humidity streams into Botrytis-relevant prediction models indicates usable methodology for FreshPak's two seasons of logs and destination inspection reports.

cooperationScope.text: Scope: a film-specification and trial-design project using FreshPak's lab (OTR/CO₂TR, headspace gas, seal strength) and historic shipment data, with milestones (a) translation of logs into a temperature/humidity profile, (b) modelled headspace and Botrytis risk ranking for a short candidate film list, (c) simulated-transit trial protocol and its execution, (d) pre-season consignment check.
Engagement form to agree: joint project and/or industrial PhD co-supervision, consistent with the researcher's stated openness.

validation.text: Baseline: current lidding film and seal pressure run in the simulated-transit protocol, recording visible Botrytis incidence at days 9 and 14 and headspace O₂/CO₂. Candidate films are measured the same way, with model-predicted versus observed equilibrium gas composition compared per film and fill weight. Go/no-go: advance to the pre-season consignment check only if the best candidate reaches the agreed mould-incidence threshold and its observed headspace trend is consistent with the model; otherwise revise film, seal setting or pre-cooling before the season deadline.

constraints.text: Required inputs from FreshPak: the two current film grades and their measured OTR/CO₂TR, standard punnet geometry and fill weight, seal pressure range, two seasons of temperature/humidity logs and destination inspection reports, and lab time for headspace and seal testing. Engagement is limited to the researcher's lab and part-time involvement; no large external testing programme can be assumed given the stated budget.

What remains outside the supported scope: heat-seal and anti-fog film behaviour, micro-condensation control in the 125 g rPET shell, compostable-material migration, and full commercial deployment or a contractual one-percent mould guarantee.

unknowns.text: Open questions: which factor dominates visible mould (field inoculum, pre-cooling delay, condensation, atmosphere imbalance); how anti-fog chemistry and seal integrity interact with condensation; whether simulated transit reproduces German/Netherlands destination outcomes; and whether any candidate film can reach <1% at day 14 within budget.
